raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Use EngramStore as the unified storage abstraction for all supported Engram model families: DeepSeek V4.1, Qwen4-Exp, LongCat Ngram, and Gemma3n/Gemma4.

Models provide row IDs and interpret returned bytes through one table contract. Shared adapters in `mem_cache/engram/` own storage integration, while each model retains its hashing, scales, projections, request history and distributed communication. Model-side changes are limited to selecting the shared adapter.

EngramStore supports local and remote storage backends through the same abstraction. This PR integrates local storage, including CUDA streams, Qwen prefetch and CUDA graph replay. **This is the companion integration for [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4701](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4701) and requires a CUDA-enabled build of that PR.** The two PRs provide the storage backend and model integration respectively, and were tested together end to end. Related RFC: kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4692.

All five checkpoints across these four families were tested end to end with real weights. Under the controlled configurations below, **30/30 request outputs match native execution exactly**, including generated tokens and output logprobs.

## Modifications

- Add `--engram-backend native|mooncake` (default `native`) and `--engram-local-dir`.
- Put shared storage and embedding adapters in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/engram/`.
- Keep model edits small: route embedding construction through a factory, and route DeepSeek owned-row lookup through the common helper.
- Preserve model hash/history, checkpoint names, scales, projections, TP/DP/CP collectives and Qwen's existing prefetch scheduling.
- Use anonymous Mooncake-owned snapshots so worker termination leaves no named table files.
- Support normal CUDA stream ordering and graph replay without introducing a request-handle type.

Install a CUDA-enabled build of the companion Mooncake PR, then:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/gemma-3n-E2B-it \
  --engram-backend mooncake \
  --engram-local-dir /dev/shm/sglang-engram
```

The README documents ownership, warmup, immutable weights and host-memory requirements. CPU checkpoint parameters are retained in addition to the snapshot, including temporary packed rows for DeepSeek. Live table updates and remote storage are outside this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
pytest -q test/manual/test_mooncake_engram.py
# 4 passed
```

Covers BF16/FP8 lookup, scaling, shard masking, prefetch streams and graph replay. DeepSeek and Qwen adapters are compared exactly against their native gather kernels, including changed IDs across graph replays. Companion Mooncake checks: **19 table tests + 11 export tests passed**. After removing its old API, the wheel and adapter tests were rerun; the real-weight E2E results below are from the earlier run of the same model lookup path.

### Real-weight local end-to-end comparison

Same source, weights, prompts and engine configuration on both backends, changing only `engram_backend`. Six requests per checkpoint, 32 greedy output tokens each, including English, Chinese, arithmetic, repeated prompts and a 133-token prefill. Calls comprise one single request, four submitted prompts, then one longer request.

| Checkpoint | TP / EP | Identical generated token sequences | Max output logprob delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 8 / 8 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (Qwen4-Exp) | 4 / 4 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 | 4 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Gemma3n-E2B-it | 1 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Gemma4-E2B-it | 1 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |

**30/30 exact token sequences**, with CUDA graph decode exercised on all checkpoints. DeepSeek and Qwen also exercised prefill graphs; upstream disables prefill graphs for the tested Gemma/LongCat configurations. Qwen uses `ple_offload_embedding=True` on both backends, exercising its prefetch side stream.

### Reproduction settings and comparison controls

Common Engine arguments: `context_length=2048`, `chunked_prefill_size=512`, `random_seed=42`, `trust_remote_code=True`; sampling: `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=32`, `ignore_eos=True`, `return_logprob=True`, `logprob_start_len=0`, `top_logprobs_num=5`.

- DeepSeek, LongCat, Qwen: `max_total_tokens=8192`, `max_running_requests=1`, `cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1]`, `disable_overlap_schedule=True`, `sampling_backend="pytorch"`, `disable_flashinfer_autotune=True`, `watchdog_timeout=1800`.
- DeepSeek: `mem_fraction_static=0.9`, `cuda_graph_backend_decode="full"`, `cuda_graph_backend_prefill="breakable"`, `cuda_graph_bs_prefill=[128,256,512]`. Native tables on GPU via `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=0`; Mooncake tables on host.
- Qwen: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`, `ple_offload_embedding=True`, `enable_deterministic_inference=True`.
- LongCat: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`.
- Gemma models: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`, `max_running_requests=4`, `cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1,2,4]`. Gemma3n additionally uses `enable_deterministic_inference=True` and `disable_overlap_schedule=True`.

Initial unconstrained comparisons were **not** exact. Native Qwen reruns also changed token/logprob results; deterministic inference made the final comparison exact. Fixed KV capacity and serialized scheduling were used to control differences caused by available device memory and batching. These are small functional regression checks, not a benchmark-dataset accuracy claim.

The four downloaded ModelScope checkpoints were size/SHA256 verified:
- Qwen: `a1fb13bf5d53cbffcf9e7562e62579ca1fe33138`
- LongCat: `186aad32a3c788b2b677653d211c0f53b4c972f7`
- Gemma3n: `0646804ed01fdd9880d5db59d489c6db418a0a35`
- Gemma4: `00e3e80811964b8cbf6e73da57ec66baa21b9d8c`

DeepSeek reused the existing local checkpoint. Test baseline: SGLang main `abf92826ee`, Mooncake main `3aa0f716`; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1/CUDA 13.0, Transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.1, Triton 3.8.0. Eight 80 GiB devices, CUDA-reported SM90. The test environment used a resolved JIT-cache path and local Triton cache to avoid cache invalidation/stale-handle issues on the shared filesystem.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Local E2E performance

**EngramStore provides one storage interface across all five checkpoints with overall inference latency close to native SGLang in these local workloads.** In the new concurrency-1 matrix, median end-to-end request latency is within **5% of native in all 15 paired cases**. Absolute TTFT, TPOT and request latency are reported below.

Measured on the same GPUs, sequentially: **1,024 / 4,096 / 16,384 input tokens, 128 output tokens, concurrency 1, 5 warmup requests and 20 measured requests per case and backend**. This gives **600 measured requests** in total. Each pair uses identical deterministic synthetic input-token sequences, verified by hashes; prefix reuse is disabled.

Values are medians over 20 requests, shown as **native → Mooncake**. Parenthesized percentages are **Δ = (Mooncake / native − 1) × 100%**, computed from unrounded measurements and rounded to two decimal places. Negative latency/TTFT/TPOT means faster; positive means slower. For memory, negative means less usage; for throughput, positive means more tokens/s. `±0.00%` denotes a change rounding to zero, not an error bar. P10–P90 ranges remain absolute values. TTFT includes Engine scheduling, IPC and streaming detokenization. Loading, warmup, HTTP and input tokenization are excluded.

**Table placement:** DeepSeek uses **TP-sharded CPU tables on both sides** (`per_rank`, retaining TP reduction); Qwen uses **CPU PLE on both sides**, retaining prefetch. This is a different workload and host layout, so it does not explain the earlier result. The remaining difference is not established as either random noise or a speedup caused by the abstraction. #### Memory

Samples are taken after warmup before the 16k case. GPU usage is summed over the TP group with other GPUs idle; host usage is process-tree PSS. KV capacity and graph settings are matched. LongCat saves approximately **58.4 GiB** of GPU memory; Gemma3n and Gemma4 save approximately **3.7 GiB** and **4.4 GiB**, respectively. The adapter retains CPU parameters plus immutable snapshots, increasing host RAM usage.

#### Reproduction

Use `test/manual/bench_mooncake_engram.py` from the companion SGLang integration, with each backend in a fresh process:

```bash
python test/manual/bench_mooncake_engram.py \
  --model-path /models/CHECKPOINT --backend native \
  --engine-args matching-engine-args.json --output native.json \
  --input-lengths 1024 4096 16384 --output-length 128 \
  --concurrencies 1 --warmups 5 --repeats 20
# Repeat with --backend mooncake --output mooncake.json.
```

Common Engine arguments: `context_length=17408`, `max_running_requests=1`, `max_total_tokens=32768`, `chunked_prefill_size=1024`, `cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1]`, `cuda_graph_bs_prefill=[1024]`, `disable_radix_cache=True`, `stream_interval=1`, `random_seed=42`, `sampling_backend="pytorch"`, `disable_flashinfer_autotune=True`, `mem_fraction_static=0.8`, `watchdog_timeout=1800`, `trust_remote_code=True`, `log_level="info"`, local directory on `/dev/shm`; overlap scheduling enabled. Sampling is greedy, `ignore_eos=True`, with no logprob return.

- DeepSeek: TP8/EP8, `mem_fraction_static=0.9`, decode graph backend `full`, prefill `breakable`; both processes use `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1` and `SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank`.
- Qwen: TP4/EP4, `ple_offload_embedding=True`, deterministic inference enabled.
- LongCat: TP4. Gemma3n/Gemma4: TP1; Gemma3n enables deterministic inference.
- Backend order: native first for Gemma4, LongCat and DeepSeek; Mooncake first for Gemma3n and Qwen.
- Synthetic text IDs are uniform in `[256, min(32000, vocab_size))`, excluding special IDs, and differ for each request. All 600 measured requests generated 128 tokens with a one-token first streamed chunk; the harness asserts no cached input tokens.
- Eight 80 GiB NVIDIA L20Z devices, CUDA-reported SM90 and NVLink; Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.1/CUDA 13.0, Transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.1, Triton 3.8.0. Same environment, NUMA policy and resolved JIT-cache path on both sides. A libc `memfd_create` shim is used on both sides only because this Conda Python omits `os.memfd_create`.
- Tested commits: Mooncake `e3d395959eee`, SGLang `70915471caa4`. No model or storage code was changed for this rerun.

#### Output consistency in performance runs

These latency samples are not claimed as exact-output correctness tests. LongCat and both Gemma checkpoints match all 60 paired output sequences each. Qwen matches 20/20 at 1k, but 0/20 at both 4k and 16k; DeepSeek matches 7/60 across the three lengths. A diagnostic rerun of the same five 4k inputs in a fresh **native Qwen** process also matches **0/5** complete sequences from the primary native run, despite identical Engine arguments and deterministic-inference mode. That diagnostic measures 4k alone, whereas the main run measures 1k first, so it establishes non-repeatability across those invocations without isolating its cause. The diagnostic is additional to the 600-request performance matrix and does not replace its samples.

Generated-token differences can also affect later decode work. The earlier controlled 30/30 token/logprob checks remain the correctness evidence for their stated settings; they do not establish exact long-context behavior under these performance settings.

This experiment supports comparable latency for the measured local workload; it is not a formal equivalence test or a dataset accuracy evaluation. Remote, HTTP serving, multimodal inputs and sustained arrival-rate workloads are outside this measurement.

</details>

<details>
<summary>TTFT investigation: repeatability, table layout and profiling</summary>

The lower DeepSeek TTFT in the main matrix is **not a demonstrated, stable EngramStore speedup**. A fresh-process **4k-only** follow-up reversed backend order (Mooncake first, native second), using the same Engine arguments, TP-sharded CPU placement, 128 output tokens, 5 warmups and 20 measured requests per backend. Paired input hashes match. Unlike the main matrix, this follow-up does not run the 1k case first.

| Metric | Native | Mooncake | Change vs native |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TTFT median (ms) | 447.48 | 449.21 | **+0.39%** |
| TTFT P10–P90 (ms) | 446.03–464.05 | 446.95–459.02 | — |
| TPOT median (ms/token) | 7.484 | 7.516 | **+0.43%** |
| Request latency median (ms) | 1397.93 | 1403.55 | **+0.40%** |

The approximately **0.4%** differences are close. The earlier 4k TTFT medians were 496.26 → 459.80 ms; the larger apparent advantage did not repeat. A bootstrap interval over this follow-up's 20 requests gives a TTFT median ratio of approximately 0.996–1.011; it does not estimate variation across independent server launches.

#### Controlled lookup experiment

A separate single-GPU experiment holds data, IDs and memory backing constant: 48,000,771 rows, 256 FP8 weight bytes plus 8 E8M0 scale bytes per row, 24 IDs per token, and 1/8 expected shard ownership. It uses CUDA graph replay, different random IDs per trial, L2 flushing, randomized variant order, 5 discarded trials and 40 measured trials, with exact output checks. Both layouts use anonymous mappings; this intentionally isolates layout from production file-mapping differences.

Percentages in each lookup column use the **native fused lookup with the same page backing** as the reference; lower is faster.

| Complete lookup path, 1024 tokens | Ordinary pages (μs) | Approximately 100% huge-page backing (μs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Native fused gather/dequantization, separate payload and scales | 200.46 (reference) | 186.69 (reference) |
| Same native arithmetic adapted to packed row strides | 123.22 (**-38.53%**) | 123.10 (**-34.06%**) |
| Current Mooncake packed gather plus GPU dequantization/masking | 193.71 (**-3.37%**) | 193.15 (**+3.46%**) |

Packing helps the native kernel in this controlled experiment, but the current Mooncake path also performs extra GPU operations. Its **complete lookup cost is close to native**, and the ordering changes with page backing. These microbenchmarks exclude TP collectives, scheduler overhead and real-model computation; they do not explain a several-percent E2E advantage by themselves.

#### Runtime observations and limits

- Both E2E backends use the same five prefill chunks for 4k: 1024, 1024, 768, 768, 512.
- Native huge-page coverage changed across launches without a code/configuration change. The original run had partial coverage for one Engram layer and almost none for the other; the follow-up reported approximately 100% for both layers on all eight ranks. This host runs kernel 5.10; its explicit `MADV_COLLAPSE` attempt returns `EINVAL`. The separately measured page-policy effect is too small to attribute the old E2E difference solely to that observation.
- After the timed runs, one 4k/one-output-token request per backend was profiled separately on all eight ranks. On TP0, native fused Engram gather kernels total about 1.65 ms; Mooncake byte-gather kernels total about 1.14 ms, **excluding Mooncake's subsequent GPU dequantization/masking**, so those two kernel totals are not equivalent complete-path comparisons. Main-model compute, collectives and GPU execution gaps occupy much more time. The profiled spans were about 0.52–0.53 s; profiler overhead means they must not replace the unprofiled timings above.
- The earlier run has no corresponding trace. Changing run order, startup memory state and prior request history together does not isolate a single cause. The evidence is consistent with run-dependent system state and timing effects, and supports reporting **comparable local performance**, not a causal TTFT speedup.
- This is an additional 40-request performance diagnostic, not a correctness pass: 4/20 complete generated sequences matched between its two backends. The controlled correctness checks and their limits remain documented above.

The layout/profile diagnostics used SGLang `70915471caa4` and the unchanged Engram implementation from Mooncake `e3d395959eee`. The subsequent directory-only move `7d817b57` preserves all three native source files byte-for-byte and was validated with a rebuilt CUDA wheel.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Earlier 128/1024-token, concurrency 1/4/16 experiments (different configuration)</summary>

These earlier measurements are retained for reference and are not pooled with the concurrency-1 matrix above. In particular, their DeepSeek native baseline uses shared host tables rather than per-rank shards. The earlier approximately 30% TTFT difference has no isolated causal explanation.

Compared native SGLang storage with Mooncake local on the **same GPUs, sequentially**, using real weights for all five checkpoints. The primary matrix has 128/1024 input tokens, 128 output tokens and concurrency 1/4/16, with 2 warmup waves and 5 measured waves per case: **210 measured requests per backend per checkpoint, 2,100 in total**.

The workload uses different deterministic synthetic text-token IDs each wave (uniform IDs in `[256, min(32000, vocab_size))`, excluding special IDs). Paired input hashes match. Timings include Engine scheduling, IPC and streaming detokenization; they exclude HTTP, input tokenization, loading and warmup. This is a closed-wave benchmark, not a sustained-arrival serving SLA or a dataset accuracy evaluation.

**The primary matrix shows throughput changes between -2.6% and +3.1%, but does not establish universal performance equivalence.** Five waves per case provide limited coverage, and short-input TTFT is sensitive to scheduling. Additional LongCat checks below expose an important exception.

#### Follow-up checks

- **LongCat, independent requests, concurrency 4, 20 measured waves after 3 warmups, reversed backend order:** at 128 input tokens, throughput changed **-6.8%** and TTFT **+39.4%**; at 1024 input tokens, throughput changed **-0.3%** and TTFT **-0.3%**. Logs show that short-input requests can be split into multiple prefill batches, with different split frequencies between runs.
- **LongCat, 128 input tokens/concurrency 4, colocated batch submission, 20 measured waves after 3 warmups:** both backends processed all 23 waves as one 4-request prefill each. Throughput was **905.6 → 897.7 tokens/s (-0.9%)**, TPOT **3.714 → 3.713 ms**, and TTFT **90.6 → 97.3 ms (+7.4%, +6.7 ms)**. Controlling arrivals removes most of the throughput gap, but a residual first-token cost remains. Both the original and controlled results are reported; this is not a zero-overhead claim.
- Performance runs retain overlap scheduling and can produce different generated sequences. **DeepSeek's native implementation was itself non-repeatable:** a separate rerun of the same five 1024-token, concurrency-1 inputs matched **0/5 complete sequences** from the first native run. Therefore these performance outputs are not claimed as exact correctness checks. The separately controlled 30/30 token/logprob checks above remain the correctness evidence.

#### Table placement and memory

DeepSeek uses native **shared host tables** versus Mooncake **TP-sharded host snapshots**. Native shared lookup avoids the TP reduction used by the sharded adapter, so this comparison includes that layout/communication difference. Qwen uses native pinned-host PLE versus Mooncake host snapshots, preserving prefetch in both. LongCat and Gemma use **native GPU tables** versus Mooncake host snapshots; those comparisons include host offloading.

Steady-state memory below is sampled before the final case after warmup. GPU memory is summed across the model's TP group (other GPUs were idle); host memory is process-tree PSS. KV capacity is fixed across backends.

| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | 353.4 → 351.1 (**-0.66%**) | 220.2 → 409.5 (**+85.99%**) |

detail.body:
## Motivation

Use EngramStore as the unified storage abstraction for all supported Engram model families: DeepSeek V4.1, Qwen4-Exp, LongCat Ngram, and Gemma3n/Gemma4.

Models provide row IDs and interpret returned bytes through one table contract. Shared adapters in `mem_cache/engram/` own storage integration, while each model retains its hashing, scales, projections, request history and distributed communication. Model-side changes are limited to selecting the shared adapter.

EngramStore supports local and remote storage backends through the same abstraction. This PR integrates local storage, including CUDA streams, Qwen prefetch and CUDA graph replay. **This is the companion integration for [kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4701](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4701) and requires a CUDA-enabled build of that PR.** The two PRs provide the storage backend and model integration respectively, and were tested together end to end. Related RFC: kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4692.

All five checkpoints across these four families were tested end to end with real weights. Under the controlled configurations below, **30/30 request outputs match native execution exactly**, including generated tokens and output logprobs.

## Modifications

- Add `--engram-backend native|mooncake` (default `native`) and `--engram-local-dir`.
- Put shared storage and embedding adapters in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/engram/`.
- Keep model edits small: route embedding construction through a factory, and route DeepSeek owned-row lookup through the common helper.
- Preserve model hash/history, checkpoint names, scales, projections, TP/DP/CP collectives and Qwen's existing prefetch scheduling.
- Use anonymous Mooncake-owned snapshots so worker termination leaves no named table files.
- Support normal CUDA stream ordering and graph replay without introducing a request-handle type.

Install a CUDA-enabled build of the companion Mooncake PR, then:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/gemma-3n-E2B-it \
  --engram-backend mooncake \
  --engram-local-dir /dev/shm/sglang-engram
```

The README documents ownership, warmup, immutable weights and host-memory requirements. CPU checkpoint parameters are retained in addition to the snapshot, including temporary packed rows for DeepSeek. Live table updates and remote storage are outside this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
pytest -q test/manual/test_mooncake_engram.py
# 4 passed
```

Covers BF16/FP8 lookup, scaling, shard masking, prefetch streams and graph replay. DeepSeek and Qwen adapters are compared exactly against their native gather kernels, including changed IDs across graph replays. Companion Mooncake checks: **19 table tests + 11 export tests passed**. After removing its old API, the wheel and adapter tests were rerun; the real-weight E2E results below are from the earlier run of the same model lookup path.

### Real-weight local end-to-end comparison

Same source, weights, prompts and engine configuration on both backends, changing only `engram_backend`. Six requests per checkpoint, 32 greedy output tokens each, including English, Chinese, arithmetic, repeated prompts and a 133-token prefill. Calls comprise one single request, four submitted prompts, then one longer request.

| Checkpoint | TP / EP | Identical generated token sequences | Max output logprob delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 8 / 8 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (Qwen4-Exp) | 4 / 4 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 | 4 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Gemma3n-E2B-it | 1 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |
| Gemma4-E2B-it | 1 / 1 | 6/6 | 0.0 |

**30/30 exact token sequences**, with CUDA graph decode exercised on all checkpoints. DeepSeek and Qwen also exercised prefill graphs; upstream disables prefill graphs for the tested Gemma/LongCat configurations. Qwen uses `ple_offload_embedding=True` on both backends, exercising its prefetch side stream.

### Reproduction settings and comparison controls

Common Engine arguments: `context_length=2048`, `chunked_prefill_size=512`, `random_seed=42`, `trust_remote_code=True`; sampling: `temperature=0`, `max_new_tokens=32`, `ignore_eos=True`, `return_logprob=True`, `logprob_start_len=0`, `top_logprobs_num=5`.

- DeepSeek, LongCat, Qwen: `max_total_tokens=8192`, `max_running_requests=1`, `cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1]`, `disable_overlap_schedule=True`, `sampling_backend="pytorch"`, `disable_flashinfer_autotune=True`, `watchdog_timeout=1800`.
- DeepSeek: `mem_fraction_static=0.9`, `cuda_graph_backend_decode="full"`, `cuda_graph_backend_prefill="breakable"`, `cuda_graph_bs_prefill=[128,256,512]`. Native tables on GPU via `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=0`; Mooncake tables on host.
- Qwen: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`, `ple_offload_embedding=True`, `enable_deterministic_inference=True`.
- LongCat: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`.
- Gemma models: `mem_fraction_static=0.7`, `max_running_requests=4`, `cuda_graph_bs_decode=[1,2,4]`. Gemma3n additionally uses `enable_deterministic_inference=True` and `disable_overlap_schedule=True`.

Initial unconstrained comparisons were **not** exact. Native Qwen reruns also changed token/logprob results; deterministic inference made the final comparison exact. Fixed KV capacity and serialized scheduling were used to control differences caused by available device memory and batching. These are small functional regression checks, not a benchmark-dataset accuracy claim.

The four downloaded ModelScope checkpoints were size/SHA256 verified:
- Qwen: `a1fb13bf5d53cbffcf9e7562e62579ca1fe33138`
- LongCat: `186aad32a3c788b2b677653d211c0f53b4c972f7`
- Gemma3n: `0646804ed01fdd9880d5db59d489c6db418a0a35`
- Gemma4: `00e3e80811964b8cbf6e73da57ec66baa21b9d8c`

### Local E2E performance

+# Unified Engram storage with Mooncake
+
+EngramStore provides one storage abstraction for N-gram/hash embeddings and
+direct token-indexed per-layer embeddings across the supported model families.
+Models provide row IDs and interpret returned bytes; storage ownership and
+lookup are shared. Its table contract supports local and remote backends; this
+SGLang integration currently selects local storage.
+
+`--engram-backend mooncake` stores lookup tables in host memory owned by
+Mooncake. `--engram-local-dir` selects the snapshot directory (default:
+`/dev/shm/sglang-engram`). Install a Mooncake build with `USE_CUDA=ON` that
+provides `mooncake.engram.EngramStore` and its private CUDA extension.
+
+```bash
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path /models/gemma-3n-E2B-it \
+  --engram-backend mooncake \
+  --engram-local-dir /dev/shm/sglang-engram
+```
+
+The default `native` backend preserves the original model implementation.
+This integration covers:
+
+| Model family | Stored table | Interpretation in SGLang |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| DeepSeek V4.1 | TP-local FP8 weights and E8M0 scales packed per row | Block dequantization; existing TP/DP/CP collectives |
+| Qwen4-Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | TP-local N-gram / PLE rows | Original table scale, convolution and request history |
+| LongCat Ngram | TP-local over-embedding rows | Original hash, projection and token history |
+| Gemma3n / Gemma4 | Per-layer input embedding rows | Original scaling, reshape, projection and gating |
+
+Hashing, tokenizer behavior, weights names and collective placement remain in
+their native model implementations. The adapters preserve the existing
+checkpoint loading attributes. Mooncake receives only row IDs and bytes.
+
+## Lifetime and memory
+
+The first eager lookup publishes an immutable snapshot of the loaded CPU
+parameters. Each table and rank gets an anonymous mapping (`persistent=False`),
+so different model instances cannot accidentally reuse stale weights. Native
+CPU parameters are retained; budget host memory for both them and the snapshot,
+plus temporary packing for DeepSeek's weights and scales. CUDA registration
+pins the snapshot pages. Disk-backed snapshots still require enough RAM for
+these pinned pages.
+
+Warm up all tables before CUDA graph capture. Lookup runs on the current CUDA
+stream, including Qwen's existing prefetch stream. Normal stream waits and
+graph dependencies provide completion ordering. No asynchronous request
+object is exposed. Destroy graphs before releasing their tables.
+
+Tables are immutable after publication: restart the engine to change these
+weights. This initial adapter does not support live weight updates or remote
+Mooncake storage. Anonymous mappings have no named snapshot files and are
+released on process exit, including when the engine kills its workers.
+
+## Tests
+

+class MooncakeVocabParallelEmbedding(VocabParallelEmbedding):
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        with torch.device("cpu"):
+            super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        if not isinstance(self.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod):
+            raise ValueError("Mooncake Engram requires an uncompressed row tensor")
+        # This method has no post-load work. Avoid the loader staging the CPU
+        # table to CUDA for quantization postprocessing.
+        self.quant_method = None
+        self._rows = ByteRows()
+
+    def _embed_local_shard(self, input_):
+        if self._rows.store is None:
+            self._rows.initialize(self.weight.detach().view(torch.uint8))
+        if self.tp_size > 1:
+            ids, mask = get_masked_input_and_mask(
+                input_,
+                self.shard_indices.org_vocab_start_index,
+                self.shard_indices.org_vocab_end_index,
+                self.shard_indices.num_org_vocab_padding,
+                self.shard_indices.added_vocab_start_index,
+                self.shard_indices.added_vocab_end_index,
+            )
+            ids = ids.masked_fill(mask, -1)
+        else:
+            ids = input_
+        with use_symmetric_memory(
+            get_parallel().tp_group, disabled=not is_allocation_symmetric()
+        ):
+            out = self._rows.lookup(ids).view(self.weight.dtype)
+            if self.output_dtype is not None:
+                out = out.to(self.output_dtype)
+        return out
+
+    def allocate_output(self, shape, device):
+        with (
+            use_symmetric_memory(
+                get_parallel().tp_group, disabled=not is_allocation_symmetric()
+            ),
+            torch.inference_mode(False),
+        ):
+            return torch.empty(
+                shape, dtype=self.output_dtype or self.weight.dtype, device=device
+            )
+
+    def gather(self, ids, out=None):
+        values = self._embed_local_shard(ids)
+        if out is not None:
+            out.copy_(values)
+            return out
+        return values
+
+    def reduce(self, output):
+        if (
+            output.numel()
+            and self.tp_size > 1
+            and not get_attn_tp_context().input_scattered
+        ):
+            if self.use_attn_tp_group:
+                return attn_tp_all_reduce(output)
+            return tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(output)
+        return output

+        if self._rows.store is None:
+            self._rows.initialize(self.weight.detach().view(torch.uint8))
+        return self._rows.lookup(input_ids).view(self.weight.dtype) * self.embed_scale

+"""Raw row storage; model hashing, quantization and collectives stay in SGLang."""
+
+import contextlib
+import logging
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ByteRows:
+    """Publish a CPU table after weight loading, then gather on the caller's stream.
+
+    Each instance owns an anonymous local snapshot, including across TP ranks.
+    Initialize during eager warmup before capturing a CUDA graph. The source
+    parameters remain available to the normal checkpoint loader.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.store = None
+
+    def initialize(self, rows: torch.Tensor):
+        from mooncake.engram import EngramStore
+
+        from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_memory
+
+        if torch.cuda.is_initialized() and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Warm up Mooncake Engram tables before CUDA graph capture"
+            )
+        if rows.device.type != "cpu" or rows.dtype != torch.uint8 or rows.ndim != 2:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Mooncake Engram initialization requires a CPU byte matrix"
+            )
+        self.row_bytes = rows.shape[1]
+        self.store = EngramStore(
+            tables={"rows": {"num_rows": rows.shape[0], "row_bytes": self.row_bytes}},
+            namespace="sglang-v1",
+            local_dir=get_memory().engram_local_dir,
+            persistent=False,
+        )
+        self.store.populate("rows", rows.contiguous().numpy())
+        logger.info("Mooncake Engram: published %s rows of %s bytes", *rows.shape)
+
+    def lookup(self, ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        indices = ids.reshape(-1, 1).contiguous()
+        output = torch.zeros(
+            (indices.shape[0], 1, self.row_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device=ids.device
+        )
+        if ids.is_cuda:
+            self.store.lookup(
+                ["rows"],
+                indices,
+                output,
+                stream=torch.cuda.current_stream(ids.device).cuda_stream,
+            )
+        else:
+            self.store.lookup(["rows"], indices.numpy(), output.numpy())
+        return output.view(*ids.shape, self.row_bytes)
+
+    def close(self):
+        if self.store is not None:
+            self.store.close()
+            self.store = None
+
+    def __del__(self):
+        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
+            self.close()
+
+
+def init_deepseek(module, block_size: int):
+    module.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.empty(module.rows, module.dim, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cpu"),
+        requires_grad=False,
+    )
+    module.scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.empty(
+            module.rows,
+            module.dim // block_size,
+            dtype=torch.float8_e8m0fnu,
+            device="cpu",
+        ),
+        requires_grad=False,
+    )
+    module._mooncake = ByteRows()
+
+
+def lookup_deepseek(module, indices: torch.Tensor, block_size: int):
+    table = module._mooncake
+    if table.store is None:
+        table.initialize(
+            torch.cat(
+                [
+                    module.weight.detach().view(torch.uint8),
+                    module.scale.detach().view(torch.uint8),
+                ],
+                dim=1,
+            )
+        )
+    local = indices - module.row_start
+    owned = (local >= 0) & (local < module.rows)
+    raw = table.lookup(local.masked_fill(~owned, -1))
+    weight = raw[..., : module.dim].contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = raw[..., module.dim :].contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+    values = weight.float().unflatten(-1, (-1, block_size)) * scale.float().unsqueeze(
+        -1
+    )
+    return values.flatten(-2).to(torch.bfloat16).masked_fill(~owned.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

+"""Measure warm Engine streaming latency and throughput for an Engram backend.
+
+Run each backend in its own process, sequentially on the same GPUs. Pass matching
+Engine arguments through --engine-args. This measures the Engine API (including
+IPC/scheduling/detokenization), without HTTP or input tokenization time.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import random
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def memory_snapshot():
+    import psutil
+
+    processes = [psutil.Process(), *psutil.Process().children(recursive=True)]
+    pss = 0
+    for process in processes:
+        try:
+            pss += process.memory_full_info().pss
+        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
+            pass
+    return {
+        "process_tree_pss_bytes": pss,
+        "gpu": subprocess.check_output(
+            [
+                "nvidia-smi",
+                "--query-gpu=index,memory.used,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm,power.draw",
+                "--format=csv,noheader,nounits",
+            ],
+            text=True,
+        ).strip(),
+    }
+
+
+async def wave(engine, prompts, output_length, batch_submit=False):
+    sampling = {
+        "temperature": 0,
+        "max_new_tokens": output_length,
+        "ignore_eos": True,
+    }
+
+    def summarize(started, first, first_count, finished, last):
+        assert first is not None and last is not None
+        count = last["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"]
+        assert count == output_length, last["meta_info"]
+        assert last["meta_info"].get("cached_tokens", 0) == 0, last["meta_info"]
+        assert count > first_count, "Need multiple streamed chunks to measure TPOT"
+        return {
+            "ttft_ms": (first - started) * 1000,
+            "latency_ms": (finished - started) * 1000,
+            "tpot_ms": (finished - first) * 1000 / (count - first_count),
+            "first_chunk_tokens": first_count,
+            "output_tokens": count,
+            "output_ids": last.get("output_ids"),
+        }
+
+    async def request(ids):
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        stream = await engine.async_generate(
+            input_ids=ids,
+            sampling_params=sampling,
+            stream=True,
+        )
+        first = None
+        first_count = None
+        last = None
+        async for chunk in stream:
+            now = time.perf_counter()
+            count = chunk["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"]
+            if count and first is None:
+                first, first_count = now, count
+            last = chunk
+        finished = time.perf_counter()
+        return summarize(started, first, first_count, finished, last)
+
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    if batch_submit:
+        states = [[None, None, None, None] for _ in prompts]
+        stream = await engine.async_generate(
+            input_ids=prompts, sampling_params=sampling, stream=True
+        )
+        async for chunk in stream:
+            now = time.perf_counter()
+            state = states[chunk["index"]]
+            count = chunk["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"]
+            if count and state[0] is None:
+                state[0], state[1] = now, count
+            state[2], state[3] = now, chunk
+        requests = [summarize(start, *state) for state in states]
+    else:
+        requests = await asyncio.gather(*(request(ids) for ids in prompts))
+    duration = time.perf_counter() - start
+    return {
+        "input_sha256": hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(prompts).encode()).hexdigest(),
+        "seconds": duration,
+        "output_tokens_per_second": sum(r["output_tokens"] for r in requests)
+        / duration,
+        "requests": requests,
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=["native", "mooncake"], required=True)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--engine-args", required=True, help="Engine arguments JSON file"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--input-lengths", type=int, nargs="+", default=[128, 1024])
+    parser.add_argument("--concurrencies", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 4, 16])
+    parser.add_argument("--output-length", type=int, default=128)
+    parser.add_argument("--warmups", type=int, default=2)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--batch-submit",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Submit each wave together using SGLang's colocated batch guard",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    assert args.output_length > 1 and args.warmups >= 1 and args.repeats >= 3
+    if args.batch_submit:
+        os.environ["SGLANG_ENABLE_COLOCATED_BATCH_GEN"] = "1"
+
+    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
+
+    import sglang as sgl
+
+    kwargs = json.loads(Path(args.engine_args).read_text())
+    kwargs.update(model_path=args.model_path, engram_backend=args.backend)
+    assert kwargs["disable_radix_cache"], "Prefix reuse invalidates cold-prefill timing"
+    assert kwargs["stream_interval"] == 1
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
+    special = set(tokenizer.all_special_ids)
+    token_pool = [
+        i for i in range(256, min(32000, tokenizer.vocab_size)) if i not in special
+    ]
+    assert token_pool
+
+    def prompts_for(length, concurrency, iteration):
+        # Different rows each wave; identical inputs for the two backends.
+        rng = random.Random(42 + length * 100000 + concurrency * 1000 + iteration)
+        return [rng.choices(token_pool, k=length) for _ in range(concurrency)]
+
+    cases = [
+        (length, concurrency)
+        for length in args.input_lengths
+        for concurrency in args.concurrencies
+    ]
+
+    output = Path(args.output)
+    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    result = {
+        "engine_args": kwargs,
+        "input_distribution": "uniform text token IDs in [256, min(32000, vocab_size)), excluding special IDs; different deterministic seed per wave",
+        "benchmark_args": vars(args),
+        "cuda_visible_devices": os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"),
+        "host_table": os.environ.get("SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE"),
+        "host_table_layout": os.environ.get("SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT"),
+        "cases": [],
+        "complete": False,
+    }
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    engine = sgl.Engine(**kwargs)
+    result["load_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - started
+    try:
+        for length, concurrency in cases:
+            for iteration in range(args.warmups):
+                prompts = prompts_for(length, concurrency, iteration)
+                engine.loop.run_until_complete(
+                    wave(engine, prompts, args.output_length, args.batch_submit)
+                )
+            before = memory_snapshot()
+            samples = [
+                engine.loop.run_until_complete(
+                    wave(
+                        engine,
+                        prompts_for(length, concurrency, args.warmups + iteration),
+                        args.output_length,
+                        args.batch_submit,
+                    )
+                )
+                for iteration in range(args.repeats)
+            ]
+            summary = {
+                "input_length": length,
+                "output_length": args.output_length,
+                "concurrency": concurrency,
+                "median_output_tokens_per_second": statistics.median(
+                    s["output_tokens_per_second"] for s in samples
+                ),
+                **{
+                    "median_" + metric: statistics.median(
+                        r[metric] for s in samples for r in s["requests"]
+                    )
+                    for metric in ("ttft_ms", "tpot_ms", "latency_ms")
+                },
+            }
+            result["cases"].append(
+                dict(
+                    summary,
+                    samples=samples,
+                    memory_before=before,
+                    memory_after=memory_snapshot(),
+                )
+            )
+            output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+            print("PERF_CASE", json.dumps(summary), flush=True)
+        result["complete"] = True
+        output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
+        print("PERF_COMPLETE", output, flush=True)
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
